telnet-open.title: Telnet enabled on port {{port}}
telnet-open.description: Telnet sends passwords and commands in clear text: anyone on the same network can read them. It is also a common target of IoT malware.
telnet-open.recommendation: Disable Telnet in the device settings and use SSH or the official app. If that is not possible, update the firmware or consider replacing the device.

ftp-cleartext.title: Unencrypted FTP on port {{port}}
ftp-cleartext.description: FTP sends credentials and files in clear text over the network.
ftp-cleartext.recommendation: Disable FTP or use SFTP / FTPS; turn the service off if it is not needed.

http-login-cleartext.title: Login page without HTTPS on port {{port}}
http-login-cleartext.description: Credentials typed in this page travel in clear text on the local network.
http-login-cleartext.recommendation: Enable HTTPS in the device settings if available and use a unique password.

tls-legacy-protocol.title: Outdated TLS protocols on port {{port}} ({{versions}})
tls-legacy-protocol.description: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and have known weaknesses.
tls-legacy-protocol.recommendation: Update the firmware or disable TLS 1.0/1.1 in the settings, keeping TLS 1.2 or 1.3.

tls-certificate-expired.title: Expired certificate on port {{port}}
tls-certificate-expired.description: The certificate presented by the device has expired: browsers show warnings and an attack becomes hard to notice.
tls-certificate-expired.recommendation: Renew or regenerate the certificate in the device settings or update the firmware.

smb-v1-enabled.title: SMB1 enabled on port {{port}}
smb-v1-enabled.description: SMB1 is an obsolete protocol exploited by well-known malware (e.g. ransomware).
smb-v1-enabled.recommendation: Disable SMB1 and use SMB2 or SMB3.

upnp-exposed-mapping.title: Port {{externalPort}} opened to the Internet via UPnP
upnp-exposed-mapping.description: The router declares an automatic forwarding (UPnP) that makes port {{internalPort}} of the device reachable from the Internet.
upnp-exposed-mapping.recommendation: Remove the forwarding from the router, disable UPnP if not needed and use the vendor's official remote access.

upnp-igd-enabled.title: UPnP enabled on the router
upnp-igd-enabled.description: Any device of the network can open ports to the Internet without asking.
upnp-igd-enabled.recommendation: Unless game consoles or apps need it, disable UPnP in the router settings.

tr069-exposed.title: TR-069 remote management port ({{port}}) reachable
tr069-exposed.description: TR-069 is used by the provider to manage the router remotely. It is usually normal, but worth knowing.
tr069-exposed.recommendation: Check with the provider that the router firmware is up to date.

rtsp-open.title: RTSP video stream on port {{port}}
rtsp-open.description: The device offers an RTSP video stream on the local network. Only a check (OPTIONS) was sent: no video was opened.
rtsp-open.recommendation: Make sure the stream requires a strong password; disable it if you do not use it.

mqtt-cleartext.title: Unencrypted MQTT on port {{port}}
mqtt-cleartext.description: MQTT messages and any credentials travel in clear text.
mqtt-cleartext.recommendation: Use MQTT over TLS (port 8883) and require authentication.

snmp-enabled.title: SNMP enabled on port {{port}}
snmp-enabled.description: SNMP can expose information about the device; no community was tried.
snmp-enabled.recommendation: Disable SNMP if not needed; otherwise use SNMPv3 with authentication.

dns-open-resolver.title: Recursive DNS server on port {{port}}
dns-open-resolver.description: A device other than the router resolves names for anyone who asks: it can be misused.
dns-open-resolver.recommendation: Check whether the DNS service is intended; disable it if not needed.

device-unknown.title: Unidentified device
device-unknown.description: It was not possible to tell what kind of device this is.
device-unknown.recommendation: Check what it is and set its category in the devices page; if you do not recognize it, consider changing the Wi-Fi password.

cve-version-match.title: {{cve}} in {{product}} {{version}}
cve-version-match.description: The version declared by the service falls within a known vulnerability.
cve-version-match.recommendation: Update the device firmware or software to the latest available version; if there is no update, restrict access to the service.

cve-product-only.title: Known vulnerabilities for {{product}} (version not determined)
cve-product-only.description: There are {{cves}} known vulnerabilities for this product, but its version is unknown: it is not possible to tell whether the device is affected.
cve-product-only.recommendation: Check the installed version in the device settings and update it if needed.

CONFIRMED_VULNERABILITY.label: Confirmed vulnerability
CONFIRMED_VULNERABILITY.explanation: The version was read from the protocol itself and exactly matches a known vulnerability.

POTENTIAL_RISK.label: Potential risk
POTENTIAL_RISK.explanation: The collected data points to a possible risk that could not be confirmed (declared version, version range or conditions to check).

SUSPICIOUS_CONFIGURATION.label: Suspicious configuration
SUSPICIOUS_CONFIGURATION.explanation: The device answered with a configuration considered unsafe.

UNVERIFIED_INFORMATION.label: Information to check
UNVERIFIED_INFORMATION.explanation: Useful information to check, not necessarily a problem.
